column3: The Hebrew says the LORD called for the famine; BSB says He decreed it.
The Hebrew separately describes her rising, acting, going, and residing; BSB condenses these actions into proceeding to act and residing.
The Hebrew calls the property her field; BSB uses her land.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew leaves the first narrator and the restorer unnamed until the later speech; BSB names Gehazi and Elisha earlier. It calls the property her field, where BSB uses her land.
The Hebrew says she recounted to him and names a eunuch; BSB says she confirmed it and uses officer.

The Hebrew leaves the man met unnamed and mentions taking the gift in his hand; BSB supplies Elisha and leaves the hand image implicit.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew leaves both men unnamed and names the face; BSB supplies Elisha and Hazael and renders the face as a gaze.
The Hebrew leaves the respondent unnamed and says sons of Israel; BSB supplies Elisha and uses Israelites.
The Hebrew calls the deed great; BSB calls it monstrous and adds mere to the dog comparison.
The Hebrew leaves the departing man unnamed; BSB supplies Hazael.
The Hebrew leaves the cloth-taker, the face-owner, and the dying man unnamed; BSB supplies Hazael, the king, and Ben-hadad.
The Hebrew explicitly mentions Jehoshaphat king of Judah in the accession setting; BSB leaves this phrase implicit and describes succeeding his father.
The Hebrew leaves the opening subject unnamed; BSB supplies Jehoram.
The Hebrew leaves the man unnamed, uses singular way, and says the daughter was his wife; BSB supplies Jehoram, uses plural ways, and describes marrying her.
The Hebrew says sons and leaves the lamp recipient pronominal; BSB uses descendants and explicitly names David.
The Hebrew leaves the ruler unnamed in the opening days phrase; BSB supplies Jehoram.
The Hebrew includes the chariot commanders among those he struck; BSB includes them among those surrounded. It says the people fled to their tents, where BSB says his troops fled to their homes.

The Hebrew repeats his fathers at the burial; BSB uses them.

The Hebrew calls Athaliah the daughter of Omri; BSB says granddaughter.
The Hebrew leaves the man unnamed and uses singular “way”; BSB supplies Ahaziah and uses plural “ways.”
The Hebrew leaves the traveler unnamed; BSB supplies Ahaziah.
The Hebrew leaves the sick man unnamed at the end and calls him sick; BSB supplies Joram and says wounded.
